question: What is foreign exchange exposure? Explain transaction, translation and economic exposure.
sources: Generally accepted international financial management principles on foreign exchange exposure
Ind AS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates (for translation of foreign operations)

points.label: Meaning
points.description: The sensitivity of a firm's cash flows, assets, liabilities or value to unexpected changes in exchange rates.
points.basis: International financial management principle: definition of currency exposure

points.label: Transaction exposure
points.description: Arises on contracted foreign currency receivables, payables, loans or orders where the rate may change between the contract date and settlement; it affects actual cash flows.
points.basis: International financial management principle: transaction exposure

points.label: Translation exposure
points.description: Also called accounting exposure; arises when the financial statements of foreign operations are translated into the reporting currency for consolidation, affecting reported figures rather than cash.
points.basis: Ind AS 21, translation of the results and financial position of a foreign operation

points.label: Economic exposure
points.description: Also called operating exposure; the effect of exchange rate changes on the present value of future operating cash flows and competitive position, even for firms with no direct foreign transactions.
points.basis: International financial management principle: economic (operating) exposure
